messages.subject: Manipulate orientation of body skeletons using R code
messages.subject_clean: Manipulate orientation of body skeletons using R code
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I have working with NeuPrintr for a while now, but recently I've started to look more into the ability to generate body skeletons of neurons using RGL. I have no issue being able to generate these skeletons, but with the work I'm doing, I'm trying to figure if there is a way to manipulate their 3D orientations solely by using code.

I have been able to automatically generate multiple images of different subsets within the 6th layer of the dorsal fan-shaped body, by using a for loop. I’ve adapted the code from the example code provided in the NeuPrintr website, and all of the skeletons generated originate in a specific orientation. I know there’s the option of manipulating their orientation by hand using the RGL 3D viewer, but I would rather not go through 20+ skeletons doing such, as that would cost a good amount of time. (I included the code as an .RTF document below, as I didn't know how to format it into this message.)

Is there any specific functions or changes to the above code that will allow me to specify certain viewpoints (i.e. rostral view of neurons) when generating these images? Any help would be appreciated.

Thank you,

Emmanuel

messages.body_plain:
Dear Emmanuel, please take a look at the command nview3d. Also rather than opening a new window with nopen3d for each plot, it is better to use npop3d to remove the last group of plotted neurons or nclear3d to clear the plot. npop3d is particularly useful if you plot a brain surface outside the loop. Finally please note that the hemibrainr package now has the option to read hemibrain meshes which can be plotted using an identical logic, but obviously look a bit nicer. All the best, Greg.

Sent from my iPhone
